summary: Custer County lookout built 1939 on Cicero Peak; decommissioned 1973-74, moved off the mountain in 1980 and shown at a Rapid City attraction until 1997. Summit now has no tower.

facts.design: 30-foot steel tower with L-4 cab, replacing an earlier wooden tower
facts.status_note: Tower taken off the mountain in 1980; no source says where it stands now, and no source describes the summit remains

staffing.status: no longer staffed after the 1973 season

access.note: National forest land; hiking road from Custer is closed to motor vehicles each year from December 15 to May 15 (SummitPost)

visit.trail_note: Rugged 1.6-mile road to the summit, per SummitPost; there is no tower to climb

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Black Hills National Forest

events.note: Firelookout and a 1939 newspaper item give 1939; the register and Wikipedia give a 1939-1940 span
Elmer Jorgenson named as lookout in 1939 coverage
Forest Lookouts lists 1973 as the final season of staffing; Wikipedia says the tower was used until 1974
Wikipedia gives March 19, 1980; Forest Lookouts gives October 1980; SummitPost gives 1980
Rapid City attraction that displayed the tower closed in 1997
Registered January 2, 2026, nominated by Dixie Boyle

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The firelookout page and the July 1939 newspaper item give 1939; the register and Wikipedia give a 1939-1940 span. The story uses 1939 and mentions the wider span.
Forest Lookouts lists 1973 as the final season and SummitPost says the tower was decommissioned in 1973; Wikipedia says it was in use until 1974. The story gives 1973 and notes the Wikipedia date.

Forest Lookouts and the register say the tower went to Marine Life in Rapid City, while SummitPost says it was sold to a private party in Custer. Removal dates are March 19, 1980 (Wikipedia) and October 1980 (Forest Lookouts). The story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Brief height 9.1 m matches the 30-foot tower in the firelookout and Forest Lookouts pages. The register's Removed field shows 1980 but the register text does not give the month. No source read says where the tower is now (Rapid City attraction, Custer buyer, or elsewhere), and none describes the summit remains; the SummitPost guide only describes the road and views. The 1967 fires come from a Rapid City Journal item quoted on Forest Lookouts, and the 1990 Cicero Peak Fire on Wikipedia is near the mountain, not tied to the lookout, so it is left out. The firelookout page gives June Johnston Stenson for 1964-1972 and the register gives June Johnston; this is probably one person and the story says only June Johnston.
